Open AI footprint and adoption.
For Lakeshore Holdings, the OpenAI footprint spans eight active use cases across 704 licensed seats with 231 active users — a portfolio-wide adoption rate of 33%.
- **Adoption is uneven, and that gap is the real story.** Two tools — Service desk ticket summarization (53%) and Treasury cash anomaly monitor (56%) — are performing well above the portfolio average, signaling where value is already landing. Six others sit between 29–35%, suggesting friction in rollout rather than resistance to the technology.
- **Readiness risk is concentrated in one place.** Contract renewal risk summarizer carries low readiness and only 8 of 28 users active — a combination that raises exposure if the tool is being relied upon for commercial decisions before it is proven.
- **Scale-or-hold decisions cannot be made on adoption data alone.** Measured business value, model risk tier, and data readiness are not yet in business context for most tools.
Caveats: source ownership and data freshness require client validation before any portfolio conclusion is final.
| Use Case / Tool | Licensed | Active | Adoption Rate | Readiness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Service desk ticket summarization | 120 | 64 | 53% | High |
| Treasury cash anomaly monitor | 16 | 9 | 56% | High |
| Brightmark proposal drafting assistant | 220 | 76 | 35% | Medium |
| Northline dispatch exception assistant | 80 | 24 | 30% | Medium |
| Great Lakes Pantry technician next-best-action | 60 | 20 | 33% | Medium |
| Portfolio KPI narrative assistant | 45 | 18 | 40% | Medium |
| Forge & Field demand sensing pilot | 35 | 12 | 34% | Medium |
| Contract renewal risk summarizer | 28 | 8 | 29% | Low |
**Branch:** Tower for ROI and scaling decisions · Intelligence for risk tradeoffs on low-readiness tools · Moves for adoption sequencing · Source for any vendor or licensing review.
